observations.observation: Git documents objects as immutable and identifies each object by a cryptographic hash of its type and contents; exact contents are recoverable by object ID only while the object has not been deleted. This separates content-addressed identity from retention.

GitHub's Git-blob API can return raw blob data for a blob SHA while that blob is available, and blob creation from supplied content returns a SHA. The endpoint is an object access/creation mechanism, not an indefinite retention guarantee.

GitHub's Git-commit endpoint reads a commit object by commit SHA and exposes the commit's tree, parents, author/committer, message and verification fields. This supports provenance capture while the object is available but does not state that a deleted/unreachable original object will remain retrievable forever.

Git's commit model binds a commit to a tree plus parent history and commit metadata. Therefore a human-readable replay package that records only a commit SHA and selected metadata is not, by itself, the full canonical object preimage needed to independently reconstruct the original commit object after deletion.

inferences: Copying the useful evidence payload and provenance into a role-local ordinary file on a separately surviving ref removes dependence on the original source branch for semantic evidence replay. Losing the original branch/reference does not erase the copied package merely because its provenance names that original ref.

This is a bounded pass for replay of the evidence package itself, conditional on the package's own repository ref remaining live and readable. It is not a claim that GitHub retains unreachable objects indefinitely.

A package that stores only the original SHA, URL and parsed metadata preserves a provenance claim but cannot independently prove or resurrect the original Git object after that object is deleted. Exact object-identity verification after deletion requires capture of the exact object preimage (object type plus canonical content, and for a full commit snapshot the referenced tree/blob payload needed by the replay claim) before loss.

The useful scheduled-Chat evidence-handoff outcome therefore does not need object resurrection: semantic replay can pass with the copied package. The stronger original-object resurrection/cryptographic-identity guarantee remains an unresolved child until a raw-preimage package is captured and replay-verified under the same zero-dependency gates.
uncertainty: No destructive deletion test was run against a disposable repository object in this slice.

This slice does not establish the smallest sufficient canonical byte set for every Git commit/signature variant; it establishes only that SHA-plus-selected-metadata is insufficient for independent post-deletion object reconstruction.

The pass is scoped to loss of the original evidence/source ref while the role-local package's own ordinary repository ref remains present. Loss of the package's own last ref re-enters the unreachable-object retention problem tested in p1-sa-605.

hard_gates.conflict_check: No O/O-derived, downstream, other-worker semantic input, shared ledger, or scheduler mutation was used. Semantic inputs were the frozen sanitized root/config, own p1-sa-605 state, and public Git/GitHub documentation.
